An attacker who knew a victim's password could obtain a full authenticated session by submitting that password through the OpenID connect flow instead of the normal login form, bypassing TOTP and WebAuthn checks entirely.

The same request could attach an attacker-controlled OpenID identifier to the victim's account before sign-in completed. Because the OpenID sign-in path also lacked a second-factor check, the attacker could subsequently authenticate using that identifier alone — without the victim's password or second factor. Changing the victim's password did not remove the linked identifier.

OpenID sign-in is enabled by default on instances set up through the installer.

## Affected Versions

Confirmed on **1.27.1**. All versions that expose the OpenID connect endpoint and support TOTP or WebAuthn second factors should be assumed affected until verified otherwise.

## Impact

**Who was affected:** Users on instances with OpenID sign-in enabled who had enrolled TOTP or WebAuthn as a second factor.

**What broke:** Second-factor enrollment is intended to make a leaked password survivable. The OpenID connect path removed that protection for enrolled users. Password-based login continued to enforce the second-factor challenge as expected.

**Persistent access:** The connect handler wrote the attacker's OpenID identifier to the victim's account before granting the session. Subsequent OpenID sign-ins using that identifier required neither the victim's password nor a second factor. Password rotation did not revoke this access; the linked identifier had to be removed manually from account settings.

**`TWO_FACTOR_AUTH = enforced` did not mitigate this.** The enforced setting relied on a session flag set at sign-in time. Because enrolled users were flagged as having completed second-factor setup, hijacked sessions passed the enforced check rather than being challenged again.

| Attack vector | Prerequisites | Consequence |
|---------------|---------------|-------------|
| OpenID connect with password | Victim's password; OpenID sign-in enabled | Full session without second-factor challenge |
| OpenID sign-in via linked identifier | Prior successful connect attack | Full session without password or second factor; survives password change |

On a compromised Gitea account, an attacker gained access to repositories, CI secrets, Actions configuration, and push permissions for everything the user could write to. Administrator accounts exposed the entire instance.

## Root Cause

`ConnectOpenIDPost` (`routers/web/auth/openid.go`) authenticated the user with `auth.UserSignIn`, discarded the returned authentication source (which carries the second-factor policy), linked a new OpenID identifier to the account, and called `handleSignIn` — none of which consulted TOTP or WebAuthn enrollment.

The password login handler (`SignInPost` in `routers/web/auth/auth.go`) checked `TwoFactorShouldSkip()`, TOTP enrollment, and WebAuthn registration before granting a session. Those checks were absent from the OpenID connect flow.

OpenID 2.0 identities are stored in the `user_openid` table rather than as a configurable authentication source, so there was no per-source setting that could explain the missing enforcement.", "ghsa_id": "GHSA-8xjr-x7rg-hp5h", "html_url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/security/advisories/GHSA-8xjr-x7rg-hp5h", "identifiers": [{"type": "GHSA", "value": "GHSA-8xjr-x7rg-hp5h"}, {"type": "CVE", "value": "CVE-2026-73535"}], "private_fork": null, "published_at": "2026-08-14T16:34:46Z", "publisher": {"avatar_url": "https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/75789103?v=4", "events_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/events{/privacy}", "followers_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/followers", "following_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/following{/other_user}", "gists_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/gists{/gist_id}", "gravatar_id": "", "html_url": "https://github.com/bircni", "id": 75789103, "login": "bircni", "node_id": "MDQ6VXNlcjc1Nzg5MTAz", "organizations_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/orgs", "received_events_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/received_events", "repos_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/repos", "site_admin": false, "starred_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/starred{/owner}{/repo}", "subscriptions_url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni/subscriptions", "type": "User", "url": "https://api.github.com/users/bircni", "user_view_type": "public"}, "severity": "high", "state": "published", "submission": null, "summary": "2FA bypass and persistent account takeover via OpenID identity linking", "updated_at": "2026-08-14T16:34:46Z", "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/go-gitea/gitea/security-advisories/GHSA-8xjr-x7rg-hp5h", "vulnerabilities": [{"package": {"ecosystem": "go", "name": "gitea.dev"}, "patched_versions": "1.27.2", "vulnerable_functions": [], "vulnerable_version_range": "<= 1.27.1"}], "withdrawn_at": null}
